conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep Imodium on hand if it comes back. Your appetite is improving too, which is excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We got your final culture results—MSSA, methicillin-sensitive Staph. That means nafcillin is the right choice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So not the super-resistant kind?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. MSSA is easier to treat. You’re lucky it wasn’t MRSA.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re almost ready for discharge. The plan is to send you to ___ Rehab Center tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will someone there help me with the IV?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, nurses will give you the nafcillin every four hours. They’ll also monitor the PICC site for infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And when does the PICC come out?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: After two weeks of antibiotics—around November 27th. The rehab team will arrange removal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final check-up. Your vitals are stable, no fever, and you’re walking well. Discharge is set for 10 a.m.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous about the rehab place. I’ve never been.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But they’re experienced with post-infection care. You’ll have therapy and support. And your family can visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My boyfriend and mom will be glad to hear I’m improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well. Keep taking your meds, watch for redness or swelling at the PICC site, and call if you develop fever again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Before you go, here’s your discharge summary. You’re leaving with a diagnosis of MSSA bacteremia from your chest port.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll finish antibiotics at the rehab center?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, two more weeks of IV nafcillin. Then the PICC line comes out. Follow up with your PCP and ID specialist in four weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. I just want to get back to my normal life.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re on the right path. Keep up the good work. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll make sure your records are sent to the rehab center. Have a safe transfer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll call my mom when I get there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a great idea. She’ll be happy to hear you’re doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel so much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s what we like to hear. Keep focusing on recovery. You’ve got this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll be in touch with your outpatient team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The transport team will be here shortly. Safe travels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll keep in touch with my doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s the best thing you can do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m feeling hopeful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And you should. You’ve made great progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks for not giving up on me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Never. We’re all part of your team. Keep going.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you soon, I hope—just for follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe journey.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Bye for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye. We’ll be checking in with your rehab team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure they know how helpful you’ve been.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That means a lot. Take care and get well.
